name: WEC Energy Group, Inc.
employees: 7,150 (2025 Annual Report inside cover); 'approximately 7,000' in every 2026 results release
summary: BOTTOM LINE UP FRONT: WEC Energy Group is the utility that turned two named hyperscale campuses — Microsoft's Mount Pleasant (2.6 GW of demand forecast through 2030, first building operating since April 2026) and the Vantage/OpenAI/Oracle 'Lighthouse' Stargate campus at Port Washington (1.3 GW through 2030, up to 3.5 GW) — into a commission-approved tariff before either drew full load: the Public Service Commission of Wisconsin approved We Energies' Very Large Customer and Bespoke Resources tariffs on April 24, 2026 (written order May 21, Docket 6630-TE-113) at a 100 MW threshold, a 15-year minimum term, 100 percent cost responsibility for dedicated generation and transmission, a fixed 10.48–10.98 percent return on 57 percent equity, and security equal to net book value for any customer rated below A-/A3 — the rule that put Oracle (BBB- since July 9, 2026) into court and then into compliance — while the $37.5B 2026–2030 plan builds 3,300 MW of combustion turbines, 2,130 MW of utility-owned batteries ($2.9B), 3,850 MW of solar and a 60 percent share of American Transmission Company's $4.1B of data-center and regional lines. BACKGROUND. Milwaukee; NYSE: WEC. A Wisconsin holding company for We Energies (Wisconsin Electric Power Company and Wisconsin Gas), Wisconsin Public Service, Peoples Gas and North Shore Gas (Chicago), Michigan Gas Utilities, Minnesota Energy Resources and Upper Michigan Energy Resources — about 1.7 million electric and 3.0 million gas customers, 8,375 MW of generating capacity and 7,150 employees (2025 Annual Report) — plus We Power (leased plants), WEC Infrastructure (2,654 MW of non-utility renewables under contract to Microsoft, Google, Meta, Tesla and others) and 60 percent of ATC. FY2025 adjusted EPS was $5.27 on revenue of $9,800M; 2026 guidance of $5.51–$5.61 was reaffirmed on July 29, 2026 with 7–8 percent long-term growth; the company expects electric demand in its territory to rise about 45 percent over 2026–2030, and the September 2026 investor book puts VLC and bespoke assets at 15 percent of the 2030 asset base. Wisconsin has no integrated resource plan regime — every plant is a separate certificate docket — and no large-load statute (four 2026 bills died), so the tariff and the PSCW's Evers-appointed commissioners are the whole framework. Collection gap: the FY2025 Form 10-K cover and Item 1 were not readable (SEC hosts blocked; the Annual Report PDF carries the financial statements but not the human-capital line), so the employee figure is the annual report's; the PSCW's May 21, 2026 order text, the VLC tariff sheets, the Microsoft agreement's megawatts, the minimum-bill percentage and ramp terms were not retrievable from the commission's ERF system; no battery or turbine OEM is named in any source; and peak demand was not found.
ecosystemRole: We assess WEC as the corpus's cleanest example of the 'bespoke resource' model — the data-center customer subscribes to specific new generation and pays its full cost for 15 years at a fixed return, and the utility builds and owns it — which makes We Energies a direct, rate-based buyer of the batteries and turbines the data centers require rather than a PPA counterparty. Basis: the PSCW's April 24, 2026 press release and WEC's September 2026 investor book (VLC and bespoke assets 15 percent of the 2030 asset base; 2,130 MW of batteries and 3,300 MW of combustion turbines in the plan). For the storage sellers in this file the doors are the build-transfer purchases from Invenergy (Paris, Darien, Koshkonong, Dawn Harvest) and the not-yet-filed ~1,500 MW balance of the battery plan, with the supplier undisclosed on every project; for the gas vendors it is the 1,100 MW Oak Creek combustion turbines (approved May 2025, in service late 2027), the 128 MW Paris reciprocating engines, and the 270 MW Foundry Ridge and 1,125 MW Red Oak Ridge turbines pending decision in the fourth quarter of 2026, again with no OEM named. For the hyperscalers and developers in the corpus WEC is Microsoft's and Vantage's utility and, through ATC, the transmission owner whose Mount Pleasant cost-allocation agreements Microsoft is protesting at FERC (ER26-3265) — the first case in this file where a hyperscaler is both a utility's tariff customer and its federal-docket adversary.

productsAndServices.name: Regulated retail electric service — We Energies and Wisconsin Public Service, and the Very Large Customer and Bespoke Resources tariffs
productsAndServices.description: Wisconsin Electric Power Company (We Energies, southeastern and eastern Wisconsin), Wisconsin Public Service (northeastern Wisconsin) and Upper Michigan Energy Resources serve about 1.7 million electric customers from 8,375 MW of generating capacity (2025 Annual Report); the Wisconsin segment's 2025 retail deliveries were 33 percent large commercial and industrial, of which data centers were 1 percent — the data-center load is almost entirely prospective. Rates are set by the PSCW in biennial cases: the 2027–2028 cases (5-UR-112 for Wisconsin Electric and Wisconsin Gas; 6690-UR-129 for WPS) were filed April 1, 2026 asking 4.7 percent and 4.5 percent for We Energies electric at a 9.9 percent return on equity, with orders expected in the fourth quarter of 2026; the filing says data centers will pay about $1.9B of 2027–2028 costs under the 'Customer Protection Plan'. The Very Large Customer tariff and its companion Bespoke Resources tariff (Docket 6630-TE-113, filed March 31, 2025; verbal approval April 24, 2026; written order May 21) apply to customers with 100 MW or more of forecast new load (the PSCW lowered the proposed 500 MW threshold): the customer subscribes to a portion of one or more dedicated new generation resources for a minimum initial term of 15 years (raised from 10), 20 years for wind and solar and the depreciable life for gas and battery assets, at a return on equity fixed for the term at 10.48–10.98 percent on a 57 percent equity ratio, excluded from future rate cases and the earnings-sharing mechanism; the commission removed the proposed 'capacity-only' option under which a customer would pay 75 percent of generation cost, leaving only the full-benefits model at 100 percent; early termination requires payment of the remaining net book value to the extent assets cannot be repurposed; and a customer rated below A- (S&P) or A3 (Moody's), or failing a tangible-net-worth and liquidity test, must post security equal to the net book value of the investments made to serve it, with the utility's waiver ability removed. Before approval, We Energies used payment-and-cancellation agreements obliging the customer to reimburse all project costs, including ATC's, if it terminated, reduced its load or approval was not received.
highlights: VLC tariff (6630-TE-113): ≥100 MW; 15-year minimum term; 100 percent of dedicated generation and transmission cost; ROE 10.48–10.98 percent and 57 percent equity fixed for the term; security at net book value below A-/A3

Microsoft signed its 15-year VLC service agreement on July 16, 2026 (subscribing at least to Red Oak Ridge; megawatts undisclosed); Vantage/Oracle move from payment-and-cancellation agreements to VLC service agreements on June 1, 2027

Oracle sued the PSCW over the collateral rule on June 24, 2026 (Ozaukee County 2026CV256) and dropped the suit on August 17; WEC's September book says Oracle 'has met the financial security requirements'; the PSCW declined the We Energies/Vantage/Cloverleaf rehearing petition in early July

The utility's own estimate: without the tariff, serving the data centers would cost other customers about $1.5B (BizTimes, February 2026); VLC customers contributed +$0.03 of EPS in Q2 2026, the first quantified margin
2027–2028 rate cases (5-UR-112, 6690-UR-129) filed April 1, 2026; orders expected Q4 2026
productsAndServices.positioning: The only large-load tariff in this corpus built as a resource subscription rather than a minimum-demand charge: Dominion's GS-5 and AEP Ohio's tariff protect other customers with 85 percent minimums on system service, while We Energies' VLC makes the customer pay for named plants at a return fixed above the utility's base ROE. The A-/A3 security test is the strictest credit rule in the file and the one Oracle's downgrade tested.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Commission-approved tariffs; VLC service agreements negotiated per customer and subscribed to specific Bespoke Resources dockets; payment-and-cancellation agreements bridge the period before approval
targetSegments: Residential, commercial and industrial customers in Wisconsin and the Upper Peninsula
Data-center campuses of 100 MW or more (Microsoft, Vantage/Oracle) and 400–500 MW prospects in discussion
productsAndServices.roadmap: PSCW rate orders Q4 2026; Vantage/Oracle VLC service agreements effective June 1, 2027; FERC decision on the ATC/We Energies Mount Pleasant agreements (ER26-3265); the PSCW's adjustment mechanism and reporting requirements added in the order

productsAndServices.name: Data-center demand — Microsoft Mount Pleasant and the Vantage/OpenAI/Oracle Port Washington campus
productsAndServices.description: WEC publishes no signed-versus-inquiry ladder; it reports 'forecasted demand through 2030' by campus. Per the September 4, 2026 investor book: Microsoft's Mount Pleasant campus in Racine County ('Fairwater') — a $20B-plus program ($7.3B for phases 1–2 and $13B more; the village approved up to 15 additional data centers on two new campuses in January 2026) — is forecast at 2.6 GW through 2030, raised from 2.1 GW in February 2026 when $1.0B was added to the capital plan and the first building began operating in April 2026 ahead of schedule; the Vantage Data Centers 'Lighthouse' campus at Port Washington, Ozaukee County, announced October 22, 2025 as a Stargate site for OpenAI and Oracle ($15B-plus, four buildings on 672 of about 1,900 acres, close to a gigawatt of AI capacity, first building possibly late 2027, completion 2028) is forecast at 1.3 GW through 2030 with site potential up to 3.5 GW, and Vantage 'is underwriting 100% of the power infrastructure investment with a dedicated electricity rate' plus at least $175M of regional infrastructure. Together they are 3.9 GW, about 45 percent of the company's electric demand over 2026–2030, and the September book projects Wisconsin electric sales growth of 6–8 percent a year over 2028–2030. On the July 29, 2026 call the CEO described three or four further prospects of 400–500 MW each with a possible announcement by year-end, and in May said existing approved sites could add 4–5 GW beyond the five-year plan. EEI's September 11, 2026 list carries both campuses ('Power up to 2,600 MW supporting the data center and additional load in SE Wisconsin'; '$15 billion, 1,300 MW … Stargate'). Meta's Beaver Dam campus, sometimes grouped with them, is Alliant Energy's load.
highlights: Microsoft Mount Pleasant: 2.6 GW through 2030; phase 1 operating April 2026; construction of the first building finished June 2026; 2,200-plus acres; ATC upgrades of more than $500M

Vantage/OpenAI/Oracle Port Washington: 1.3 GW through 2030, up to 3.5 GW; $15B-plus; ATC's transmission project refiled September 18, 2026 at $2.48–2.72B including about $1.1B of Oracle-funded stabilization at the Decker substation; the local TID lawsuit dismissed September 22, 2026
Total 3.9 GW = ~45 percent demand growth 2026–2030; VLC/bespoke assets 15 percent of the 2030 asset base
Prospects: 3–4 customers of 400–500 MW each in discussion; 4–5 GW of further potential at approved sites (CEO, May and July 2026)
productsAndServices.positioning: Smaller than Dominion's, Duke's or AEP's books in gigawatts but the most fully contracted in structure — both campuses sit under a dedicated tariff and the larger one has a signed 15-year agreement — and the most concentrated: two customers are the whole story, as at DTE.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: VLC service agreements and payment-and-cancellation agreements; ATC large-load project commitment agreements for the transmission
targetSegments: Hyperscalers building owned campuses in southeastern Wisconsin
Colocation developers with an anchor tenant (Vantage for Oracle/OpenAI)
productsAndServices.roadmap: A possible third announcement by year-end 2026; Port Washington's first building late 2027; Mount Pleasant's second building 2028; the ATC line decision expected by year-end 2026 per WEC

productsAndServices.name: Utility-owned battery storage — 2,130 MW ($2.9B) in the 2026–2030 plan, bought build-transfer from developers
productsAndServices.description: The September 2026 investor book carries 2,130 MW of battery storage ($2.9B) inside $12.6B of regulated renewables for 2026–2030; the 10-K's three-year battery capex is $258M (2026), $413M (2027) and $254M (2028). Named projects (WEC share of capacity; all through We Energies and WPS at 90 percent with MGE at 10 percent unless stated): Paris Battery Park, Kenosha County — 110 MW total, 99 MW WEC share, four hours, Wisconsin's first large-scale battery, in service June 3, 2025 ($236.8M in the plant table); Darien, Walworth County — 68 MW of 75 MW (5-BS-255, approved; ground broken late July 2026; 2027); Koshkonong, Dane County — 149 MW of 165 MW (5-BS-258; under construction; 2027); High Noon, Columbia County — 149 MW (5-BS-276, approved April 11, 2025; 2027); Saratoga, Wood County — 45 MW of 50 MW (5-BS-280, approved November 25, 2025; 2028); Dawn Harvest, Rock County — 50 MW, Wisconsin Electric 100 percent (5-BS-281, approved March 12, 2026 with 150 MW of solar for about $443M; ground broken August 2026; 2028); and Dawn Break, Waushara County — 162 MW of 180 MW (5-BS-289, decision expected Q4 2026; 2029). The named projects sum to about 720 MW, so roughly two-thirds of the 2,130 MW plan is not yet filed. Every named battery is bought build-transfer from a developer — Invenergy for Paris, Darien, Koshkonong and Dawn Harvest, OneEnergy Renewables for the Good Oak and Gristmill solar — and no battery supplier, integrator or megawatt-hour rating beyond 'four hours' is disclosed in any document read. We Energies' own August 2026 tally is '600 MW of battery storage in service, under construction or filed'. Pilots: a CMBlu organic-flow battery with EPRI and a 20 MW Energy Dome CO2 battery at Columbia with Alliant and MGE.
highlights: 2,130 MW / $2.9B of batteries in the 2026–2030 plan; ~720 MW named with dockets; Paris (99 MW) in service June 2025
Approved 2025–2026: High Noon 149 MW, Saratoga 45 MW, Dawn Harvest 50 MW; Darien and Koshkonong under construction for 2027; Dawn Break 162 MW pending Q4 2026
Developer channel: Invenergy build-transfer (Paris, Darien, Koshkonong, Dawn Harvest, Badger Hollow wind); OneEnergy (Good Oak, Gristmill solar)
No BESS OEM disclosed; solar panels flagged in the 10-K for AD/CVD and UFLPA effects already reflected in dates and costs

Bespoke resources subscribed by VLC customers

productsAndServices.name: Dispatchable generation — 3,300 MW of combustion turbines, 180 MW of reciprocating engines, LNG storage and the Point Beach nuclear extension
productsAndServices.description: The thermal and LNG plan is $7.4B for 2026–2030: 3,300 MW of combustion turbines ($5.2B), 180 MW of reciprocating internal combustion engines ($240M), 150 MW of combined-cycle summer upgrades ($280M), coal-to-gas conversions and fuel-oil backup ($370M) and 6 Bcf of LNG storage ($1.3B). Approved on May 22, 2025: the Oak Creek combustion turbines, 1,100 MW (6630-CE-317, ~$1.2B, in service 2027–2028, under construction, with a 2 Bcf Oak Creek LNG facility and the Rochester lateral) and the Paris reciprocating engines, 128 MW in seven units (6630-CE-316, $300M, 2027). Pending with decisions expected in the fourth quarter of 2026: Foundry Ridge, 270 MW (6630-BS-103, $550M, 2028) and Red Oak Ridge, 1,125 MW (6630-BS-104, $1.7B, 2029–2030) — both Invenergy-developed sites that We Energies filed to acquire in November 2025 as part of an 'almost 3 GW', $5.5B package — plus a 100 MW turbine upgrade at the Port Washington Generating Station ($227M, 2028) and gas co-firing at the Elm Road coal units. The 611 MW Oak Creek units 7–8 are kept through end-2027 as a bridge (retirement deferred twice), Weston 3 retires in 2031, coal goes to backup-only by 2030 and out by 2032, and WEC has 'paused our near-term' carbon goals for reliability while keeping 2050 net-neutral. On the nuclear side, WEC agreed in August 2026 to extend the Point Beach purchase agreement with NextEra — about 1 GW, Unit 1 to October 2050 and Unit 2 to March 2053 — 'expected to result in savings for customers compared to the terms of the current PPA' (price escalating from $75.51/MWh in 2026 to $122.45 by 2033 under the existing contract per Wisconsin Watch); PSCW approval is being sought and pricing is not disclosed. No turbine OEM or EPC is named. There is no new gas plant at Port Washington for the data center; the campus is grid-served through the ATC line.
highlights: 3,300 MW of CTs ($5.2B) and 180 MW of RICE in the plan; Oak Creek 1,100 MW and Paris 128 MW approved May 2025, in service late 2027; Foundry Ridge 270 MW and Red Oak Ridge 1,125 MW pending Q4 2026
Point Beach PPA with NextEra extended to 2050/2053 (~1 GW), PSCW approval pending
Oak Creek 7–8 (611 MW) coal kept to end-2027 as the bridge; coal exit by 2032

productsAndServices.positioning: The gas book is peaker-heavy — combustion turbines and engines rather than combined cycle — which suits a load that is contracted to arrive over 2027–2030 and a market (MISO North) whose capacity price fell 42 percent in the 2026/27 auction; Duke and DTE, by contrast, are certifying baseload combined cycles.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Self-build under PSCW certificates (CE and BS dockets) and purchases of developer-built plants; Point Beach bought under a PPA
targetSegments: MISO reliability and the data-center ramp
Bespoke Resources subscriptions — Microsoft subscribes at least to Red Oak Ridge
productsAndServices.roadmap: Foundry Ridge and Red Oak Ridge decisions Q4 2026; Oak Creek CTs and Paris RICE on line late 2027; Point Beach extension order; Columbia 1–2 gas conversion decision

productsAndServices.name: American Transmission Company (60 percent) — the data-center lines and the FERC cost-allocation dispute
productsAndServices.description: WEC owns about 60 percent of ATC (equity-accounted), a MISO transmission owner serving more than five million consumers in Wisconsin, Minnesota, Illinois and Upper Michigan at 69–345 kV. WEC's share of ATC capital is $4.1B for 2026–2030 ($657M in 2026 rising to $901M in 2030): economic growth $1.4B, MISO long-range transmission Tranche 1 $700M and Tranche 2 $400M, with $800M more expected after 2031. ATC expects more than $2B of data-center-related transmission — more than $500M for Mount Pleasant and the Port Washington project, whose original $1.39–1.67B application (137-CE-221) had its completeness determination revoked by the PSCW (vote August 7, 2026) and which ATC refiled on September 18 at $2.48–2.72B including about $1.1B of Oracle-funded stabilization equipment at the Decker substation. On July 24, 2026 MISO filed at FERC (ER26-3265) a Minimum Transmission Charge Agreement and four amended Large Load Project Commitment Agreements between ATC and Wisconsin Electric for the Microsoft campus, under which We Energies pays ATC's network rate on 100 percent of the requested transmission capacity for 15 years from completion (capped at the project's lifetime incremental revenue requirement) and passes the cost to Microsoft; Microsoft protested on August 21 (an early-termination 'windfall', CWIP recovery, no consultation, and WEC's position as ATC's largest shareholder), joined by the PSCW's comments, the Citizens Utility Board, the Data Center Coalition and the Wisconsin Industrial Energy Group. ATC calls it 'a customer protection mechanism that follows the cost causer, cost payer methodology'. FERC's June 18, 2026 order to show cause on large-load transmission cost allocation and its RM26-4 rulemaking are the federal backdrop; MISO Tranche 2.1's Wisconsin 765 kV segments were awarded to other developers (Transource/BHE, Viridon), not ATC.
highlights: WEC share of ATC capex $4.1B (2026–2030); ATC data-center transmission more than $2B
Port Washington line refiled September 18, 2026 at $2.48–2.72B after the PSCW revoked completeness of the $1.39–1.67B application
FERC ER26-3265: 15-year minimum transmission charge for Mount Pleasant, protested by Microsoft on August 21, 2026
Electric distribution $4.7B in the plan; 72,800 miles of distribution lines
productsAndServices.positioning: The only utility in this corpus whose transmission affiliate is in a FERC fight with its own largest data-center customer; the outcome will set the pro forma for how MISO utilities pass transmission risk to large loads.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: FERC formula rates (ATC, 10.48 percent ROE on 50 percent equity) and large-load project commitment agreements passed through the VLC tariff
productsAndServices.roadmap: FERC action on ER26-3265; PSCW decision on the refiled Port Washington project (expected by year-end 2026 per WEC); Tranche 2.1 construction to 2034

productsAndServices.name: Gas distribution — Peoples Gas, North Shore Gas, Wisconsin Gas, WPS gas, Michigan and Minnesota utilities
productsAndServices.description: About 3.0 million gas customers: the Wisconsin segment's 1.5 million, Peoples Gas and North Shore Gas's 1.06 million in Chicago and its northern suburbs, and 444,000 at Minnesota Energy Resources and Michigan Gas Utilities. Gas distribution is $7.1B of the 2026–2030 plan, driven by the Illinois Commerce Commission's February 20, 2025 order ending the Peoples Gas System Modernization Program investigation and mandating retirement of cast- and ductile-iron mains by 2035 under a safety monitor, with annual spend ramping to about $500M by 2028; the ICC approved a $2.3B rider settlement 5–0 on May 21, 2026 with $130M of plant reductions and $125M of credits, and Peoples Gas's 2027 rate case (26-0065; request cut to $144M in July 2026) is due for decision in December 2026. Bluewater provides gas storage. The gas business is not a data-center counterparty except as the LNG and pipeline supplier to the new Wisconsin turbines.

ICC-mandated Peoples Gas main retirement by 2035; $2.3B rider settlement approved May 21, 2026
Peoples Gas rate order due December 2026
productsAndServices.positioning: The Illinois gas franchise is WEC's regulatory soft spot — a mandated program under a safety monitor — and unrelated to the AI-load story except as capital competition.

strategyRead: (High confidence) We assess that the Bespoke Resources structure — the data-center customer subscribes to named new plants and pays 100 percent of their cost for at least 15 years at a return fixed at 10.48–10.98 percent — makes We Energies the corpus's most direct utility buyer of the generation its hyperscalers need, and that the PSCW's modifications made the structure stricter for the customer, not the utility. Basis: the April 24, 2026 press release (100 MW threshold, 15-year minimum, capacity-only option removed, A-/A3 security) and the September 2026 investor book (VLC/bespoke assets 15 percent of the 2030 asset base). We expect the equipment for the bespoke plants — Red Oak Ridge's turbines, the unfiled ~1,400 MW of batteries — to be selected by We Energies' major-projects group and by Invenergy on the build-transfer sites, with the OEM decisions unpublished until the certificate dockets.

(High confidence) We assess that credit, not load, is the binding constraint on the Port Washington campus, and that the tariff's A-/A3 security rule has already done what it was written to do. Basis: S&P's July 9, 2026 downgrade of Oracle to BBB-; the June 12 rehearing petition by We Energies, Vantage and Cloverleaf to loosen the rule and the commission's refusal; Oracle's June 24 suit and its August 17 dismissal; WEC's statement that Oracle 'has met the financial security requirements'. The payment-and-cancellation agreements carry the campus until VLC service agreements take effect on June 1, 2027; security equal to net book value is what protects the other 1.1 million We Energies customers if Oracle's rating falls further.

(Moderate confidence) We assess that FERC's handling of the ATC–Wisconsin Electric Mount Pleasant agreements (ER26-3265) is the single most consequential open docket for WEC's model, because the VLC tariff assigns 100 percent of transmission cost to the customer and Microsoft's protest attacks exactly that assignment. Basis: the July 24 filing (15-year minimum charge on 100 percent of requested capacity), Microsoft's August 21 protest, the PSCW's own August 14 comments calling ATC's filing 'far from fully responsive', and FERC's June 18 show-cause order on large-load transmission allocation. A FERC decision that trims the early-termination or CWIP terms would shift some of the $2B-plus of data-center transmission back toward the network rate — and WEC owns 60 percent of that network.

(Moderate confidence) We assess that the 2,130 MW battery plan is real but two-thirds unfiled, and that the filing cadence — one or two 5-BS dockets a year through Invenergy — is the practical ceiling on how fast a storage seller can enter. Basis: the September 2026 investor book's named projects (about 720 MW WEC share) against the plan total; the 10-K's battery capex profile peaking in 2027; We Energies' August 2026 tally of 600 MW in service, under construction or filed. A supplier wanting the balance sells to Invenergy at bid stage or to We Energies' major-projects group for a self-build, and there is no RFP door comparable to Duke's South Carolina solicitation or DTE's annual storage RFP.

(Moderate confidence) We assess that WEC's exposure to Wisconsin politics is rising and that the 2026 gubernatorial election is the tripwire. Basis: four data-center bills died in the 2026 session (AB 840 passed the Assembly 53–44 and stalled in the Senate), moratorium proposals surfaced on the Q2 call, Kenosha residents sought a moratorium on Microsoft's second site in August, and all three PSCW commissioners are appointees of a governor whose term ends in January 2027. The tariff is an order, not a statute, and a commission with different priorities could revisit its return or its threshold in the next rate cycle.

(Low confidence) We assess that a third named campus of 400–500 MW will be announced before the February 2027 call, as the CEO has twice suggested, and that it will be a colocation developer rather than a hyperscaler. Basis: 'hopefully another announcement this fall' (May 2026) and 'prospects of 400–500 MW each' (July 2026) — sizes below a hyperscaler's own campus but above the 100 MW tariff threshold. No customer, site or filing has been found.

policyExposure.exposure: The 2026/27 planning resource auction cleared the North/Central zones, including Wisconsin, at $126/MW-day for summer, down 42 percent from $217 in 2025/26, with a 4.6 GW surplus above the reserve requirement. WEC's public rationale for keeping the 611 MW Oak Creek 7–8 coal units through 2027 and adding 3,300 MW of combustion turbines is 'tightened energy supply requirements in the Midwest power market' and MISO/NERC reliability warnings, not price; the company has 'paused our near-term' carbon goals for the same reason while keeping 2050 net-neutral. No WEC commentary on the auction price was found.
policyExposure.mitigation: Oak Creek CTs and Paris RICE in service late 2027; Oak Creek 7–8 retained as the bridge; the Point Beach extension to 2050/2053; support for MISO's expedited resource-addition queue.

policyExposure.exposure: MISO's July 24, 2026 filing of the ATC–Wisconsin Electric Minimum Transmission Charge Agreement and four amended large-load project commitment agreements for Microsoft's Mount Pleasant campus (a 15-year charge on 100 percent of requested capacity, capped at the lifetime incremental revenue requirement, for projects of $100M or 100 MW or more) is protested by Microsoft, the Citizens Utility Board, the Data Center Coalition and the Wisconsin Industrial Energy Group, with the PSCW's own comments calling ATC's filing 'far from fully responsive'. FERC's June 18 order to show cause on large-load transmission allocation (195 FERC ¶ 61,212) and its RM26-4 rulemaking set the federal frame; the CUB argues ATC's agreements should not become the pro forma template.
policyExposure.mitigation: ATC: 'a customer protection mechanism that follows the cost causer, cost payer methodology'; WEC says the Vantage line is 'in this forecast' and expects approval by year-end.

policyExposure.exposure: Net production tax credits reduced tax expense by $168.5M in the first half of 2026 (effective tax rate 6.7 percent, Q2 2026 10-Q per third-party summary); WEC Infrastructure sells PTCs under transferability; the 10-K states the 2025 federal tax law 'preserves the ability to' claim credits for storage, hydro, nuclear and other zero-emission technologies and We Energies' releases cite 'hundreds of millions of dollars' of federal credits as customer-savings drivers for the solar and battery purchases. The 10-K also flags Commerce Department AD/CVD duties on solar panels and cells from four southeast-Asian countries, further investigations (Laos, Indonesia, India) and UFLPA customs actions, with 'expected in-service dates and costs identified above already reflect some of these impacts'. No FEOC or battery-specific tariff statement was found.
policyExposure.mitigation: Build-transfer purchases shift panel and battery sourcing risk to the developer until transfer; in-service dates already reflect tariff effects per the 10-K.

policyExposure.exposure: No Wisconsin large-load or storage statute exists; the VLC tariff order is the framework. In the 2026 session AB 840/SB 843 (data-center cost and water provisions) passed the Assembly 53–44 and died in the Senate, and AB 722/SB 729, the NDA-ban bill and a moratorium bill all failed. Data centers are an issue in the 2026 governor's race (Governor Evers, who appointed all three PSCW commissioners, is not running; his term ends January 2027), Kenosha residents sought a moratorium on Microsoft's second site in August 2026, and the Wisconsin Rapids mayor has called for state rules.
